clue.text: 'Horribly boring Belarus': that'll get the citizenry worked up

definitions.text: that'll get the citizenry worked up
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for an adjective

indicators.note: done horribly, the quoted words are mangled out of their proper order

blocks.note: the thirteen letters of the quoted phrase

explanation.surface: Someone quotes a scathing verdict on Belarus as a slogan to stir up the crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech that inflames a crowd and stirs people to protest or riot is described with this compound adjective.

clue.text: Oddly rejected Fruit Shoots; took rice dish

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are thrown out, so only the even-placed ones survive

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of these words

explanation.surface: A child turns down cartons of Fruit Shoots and eats a plate of rice instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Fruit Shoots is a British brand of children's fruit drink, which makes 'rejected' read as refusing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian dish of rice cooked slowly in stock is a classic example of a rice dish.

clue.text: Half-cut, putting together tacky jewellery

indicators.note: half of the word is cut away, here the front five letters of ten

blocks.note: putting things together is assembling them

explanation.surface: A tipsy person strings together some gaudy trinkets.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for drunk, which is the picture the surface paints; here it means cut in half, dropping ASSEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashy, showy jewellery worn ostentatiously is called this in modern slang.

clue.text: Bishop's left one part of hand covered in salve

indicators.note: one item covered in another sits wrapped inside it

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
I is the Roman numeral one
the palm is the inner surface of the hand
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop has left a hand covered in ointment.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop's B goes inside PALM, giving PBALM, after L and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing waxy ointment for chapped lips is a kind of salve.

clue.text: Aristotle unsure about act of stupid bravado

indicators.note: unsure here works with about to suggest letters muddled and moved around

blocks.note: the philosopher's name supplies nine letters
this word is also part of the fodder

explanation.surface: The ancient philosopher is uncertain what to make of a reckless show of courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsure' does double duty in the surface but here its letters are fodder; 'about' alone is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinning a revolver with one bullet and firing at your own head is the archetypal reckless gamble.

clue.text: 2nd of August: Farah's entered racing event, making maximum effort

indicators.note: second of a word means take its second letter only
something that has entered another sits inside it

blocks.note: the second letter of the month
the TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
Mo Farah the British distance runner, with the 's kept

explanation.surface: On 2 August Mo Farah lines up in a race and gives it everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo Farah is the British Olympic champion at 5,000 and 10,000 metres; the Isle of Man race is known by its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing one's utmost means trying as hard as possible, the greatest degree of effort available.

clue.text: Here, one's surrounded by Asian land ... or water!?

definitions.text: Here, one's surrounded by Asian land ... or water!?

indicators.note: a thing surrounded by another is enclosed on all sides by it

blocks.note: a country in South Asia
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A puzzle of geography: in this place you are hemmed in by Asian land, or perhaps by sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: an archipelago where anyone is surrounded by Asian land or by water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Southeast Asian nation of thousands of islands leaves every inhabitant ringed by island territory or ocean.

clue.text: Vacuous gadfly speeds, goes for a spin

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word loses its middle and keeps its outside letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
speeds as a noun, as in rates of travel

explanation.surface: An empty-headed irritant races about and takes a drive.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate or whirl around a central point is to spin, the sense of 'goes for a spin' here.

clue.text: Knocked back, it's a wine from Piedmont

indicators.note: knocked back suggests sent backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: the words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone downs a glass and identifies it as a Piedmont wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' reads as drinking the wine, but it signals that 'it's a' is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: This sparkling white from the Piedmont region of northern Italy is named after the town where it is made.

clue.text: Instagram entry displaying demon: about right to get 'like' (Jeff Koons' work)

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around and rearranged

blocks.note: an item put up on Instagram is a post
fodder taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A social-media post shows a demon and earns a like, pictured as an artwork by Jeff Koons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' is not the social-media like but part of the definition: in the style of Jeff Koons, the American artist of the balloon dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Koons's kitsch, ironic sculpture is a textbook case of the late-20th-century movement that followed modernism.

clue.text: Mark a git's been given, being contrary – disgrace

indicators.note: contrary means going the opposite way, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
M abbreviates mark, the old German currency
taken as written; a git is British slang for an idiot

explanation.surface: An awkward idiot is given a black mark for his contrariness, to his shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like the verb or the definition, but it supplies only M.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of shame attached to a person or condition, which is a social disgrace.

clue.text: Senselessness involving stupidity, to start with!

definitions.text: Senselessness involving stupidity, to start with!

indicators.note: involving means taking something inside, so one word wraps another
to start with points to the opening letter of the word before

blocks.note: pointless silliness
the word's opening letter

explanation.surface: An exclamation that senseless behaviour starts with sheer stupidity.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: senselessness wrapped round stupidity is madness.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness is the state of lacking reason, so senseless stupidity taken together describes it.

clue.text: Dutch award initially rejected by German author, being big beast

indicators.note: initially takes only the first letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: D abbreviates Dutch
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
the word's opening letter
Thomas Mann, the German novelist

explanation.surface: A Dutch prize is turned down by a German writer, who seems a beast for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially rejected' looks like the award being refused, but it only supplies R.
explanation.definitionFit: This large German guard-dog breed, spelt with the double N, is a sizeable animal.

clue.text: Each lad in resort gets Mexican food

indicators.note: to re-sort letters is to sort them again into a new order

blocks.note: fodder taken as written
also part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Every young man at the holiday resort is served Mexican food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' reads as a holiday spot but means re-sort; 'in' does double duty as fodder too.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled tortilla with a filling and chilli sauce is a staple of the cuisine of Mexico.

clue.text: Letters from Greece – audible expressions of yearning

indicators.note: audible means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: long breaths of longing

explanation.surface: Letters arrive from Greece, and someone sighs with longing over them.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek letter psi is commonly said 'sigh' in English, the P silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the twenty-third character of the Greek alphabet names letters of that alphabet.

clue.text: Part of actualité?

indicators.note: part of says only a portion of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.walkthrough: The French word actualité means current affairs; a piece of news reality is the answer, which also sits inside 'of actualité'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something real and true, as opposed to opinion, is a single item of actuality.

clue.text: Prefer to include tip of liquorice, for taste

indicators.note: one word includes another by holding it inside
the tip of a word is its very first letter

blocks.note: to prefer something is to favour it
the word's opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone likes a hint of liquorice to season a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The distinctive taste of a food or drink is its characteristic savour on the tongue.

clue.text: Game hand makes you freak out

blocks.note: Go is the Japanese board game
a hand is a bunch of these fruit

explanation.surface: A dealt hand of cards drives a player wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand' suggests cards, but a hand is also a cluster of bananas on the stem.
explanation.definitionFit: To go crazy with anger or excitement is an informal idiom for losing control.

clue.text: Leaders from Antigua & Barbuda irritate king with trapped wind; this will be tricky

indicators.note: leaders are the words' front letters

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the three words
trapped wind in the gut is gas
K is the chess notation for king

explanation.surface: The Caribbean nation's leaders annoy the king, who is suffering from wind, which makes things awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: A demanding request or a hard task is informally described with this idiom of difficulty.

clue.text: Heading off, navigator defying gravity?

indicators.note: the head of the word is taken off, losing its first letter
something defying gravity rejects it, so that letter is thrown out

blocks.note: taken as written
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: Someone sets off, a navigator who manages to rise against gravity.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop N from the front and G from the middle of NAVIGATOR; the whole clue also pictures a pilot taking off.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot who steers a plane off the ground does literally defy gravity while finding the way.

clue.text: Hoo-hah about cryogenic extract

indicators.note: an extract is a piece taken out of a longer run of text

blocks.note: the letters span the two words

explanation.surface: A fuss breaks out over a sample taken from cryogenic storage.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-hah is a noisy commotion or row, and a public protest or uproar is the same thing.

clue.text: Traditional halibut prepared with aïoli

indicators.note: fish that is prepared is cut and rearranged before serving

blocks.note: the fish taken as written
just the opening letter of the garlic sauce

explanation.surface: A classic dish: halibut cooked and served with garlic mayonnaise.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first letter of 'aïoli' joins the fish's letters before they are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something customary, done by long-standing custom or routine, is both habitual and traditional.

clue.text: What Everyman's pen creates: like some Shakespearean verses

blocks.note: the setter speaking of himself: Everyman is becomes I am
Bic is a famous brand of ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: The setter boasts about the poetry his pen turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the setter refers to himself as I, so 'Everyman's' means 'I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: Much of Shakespeare's drama is in pentameter built from feet of a short syllable followed by a stressed one.

clue.text: Primarily, Mesoamerican / ancient Yucatan, architecturally notable?

definitions.text: Primarily, Mesoamerican / ancient Yucatan, architecturally notable?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so each word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A description of an old Central American civilisation famed for its buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well as spelling it from initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The civilisation of the Yucatán built remarkable stepped pyramids and temples in ancient Mesoamerica.

clue.text: In review: small bit of land where O Canada's sung, principally, alongside river!

definitions.text: In review: small bit of land where O Canada's sung, principally, alongside river!

indicators.note: a review looks back over things, so the letters are read backwards
principally means chiefly or first, taking each word's opening letter

blocks.note: an ait is a small island in a river, a British word used of the Thames
the opening letters of the three words
the Avon is a river in England

explanation.surface: Looking back on a small patch of land by a river where the Canadian anthem is sung.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a Canadian province, a piece of land where O Canada, the national anthem, is sung.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic province of Canada is a region where the Canadian national anthem is naturally sung.

clue.text: Even so, the writer's a beast

blocks.note: even so and yet both mean nevertheless
the writer is the setter speaking of himself

explanation.surface: A grudging admission: all the same, the author is a brute.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of the Himalayas is a legendary creature, an ape-like animal of folklore.

clue.text: Interpret corner key, incorrectly, as aid in calculation

indicators.note: letters placed incorrectly are out of their right order

blocks.note: to interpret something is to read it
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone misreads a key in a corner of a chart meant to help with sums.
explanation.walkthrough: A ready reckoner is a British term for a book or table of precomputed figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed table of worked-out values lets people look up results instead of doing arithmetic, so it assists calculation.
